test_categories.name: Backend
test_categories.description: REST APIs, Database design, HTTP status codes, and server-side logic.

questions.question: Which HTTP status code should be returned when a resource is successfully created via a POST request?
questions.explanation: 201 Created is the standard HTTP response status code for successful resource creation.

questions.question: What is the primary advantage of database indexing on frequently queried columns?
options: Significantly reduces query search time from O(N) to O(log N)
questions.explanation: Indexes (like B-Trees) provide fast lookup access paths, drastically speeding up SELECT queries.

questions.question: In FastAPI, what library is used under the hood for schema validation and request serialization?
questions.explanation: FastAPI is deeply integrated with Pydantic for data parsing, type validation, and documentation.

questions.question: What does ACID stand for in relational database management systems?
questions.explanation: ACID properties ensure database transactions are processed reliably.

questions.question: Which HTTP method is idempotent according to REST conventions?
questions.explanation: PUT is idempotent: multiple identical requests have the exact same effect as a single request.

test_categories.name: Cloud
test_categories.description: Containers, Docker, CI/CD pipelines, and cloud resilience.

questions.question: What is the primary difference between a Docker container and a Virtual Machine (VM)?
options: Containers virtualize the hardware; VMs virtualize the OS
Containers share the host OS kernel and are lightweight; VMs run a full guest OS
Containers only work on Linux servers; VMs only work on Windows
questions.explanation: Containers share the host operating system kernel, making them lightweight and fast to start.

questions.question: In a Dockerfile, which instruction specifies the command executed when the container starts?
questions.explanation: CMD provides defaults for an executing container, whereas RUN executes during image build time.

questions.question: What does CI/CD stand for in modern cloud software engineering?
questions.explanation: CI/CD automates code integration, testing, build artifacts, and deployment pipelines.

questions.question: What is horizontal scaling in cloud architecture?
options: Adding more CPU and RAM to a single existing server instance
Adding more server instances or containers to distribute load across a pool
Migrating all data to cold archival storage
Switching from relational SQL to non-relational NoSQL
questions.explanation: Horizontal scaling (scale out) means adding more machine nodes or container replicas to share traffic.

questions.question: Which principle is a core pillar of the Twelve-Factor App methodology for cloud applications?
options: Rely on local state in persistent disk
Execute background processes synchronously in the main thread
questions.explanation: Twelve-Factor App rule III states: store configuration in the environment, never in versioned code.

test_categories.name: AI/ML
test_categories.description: Vector embeddings, cosine similarity, data preprocessing, and model basics.

questions.question: What does a dense vector embedding represent in modern semantic AI systems?
options: A numerical vector in continuous multi-dimensional space capturing semantic meaning
A compressed zip archive of text
A binary tree structure for disk storage
questions.explanation: Vector embeddings represent text or entities as coordinates in semantic embedding space where similar concepts cluster together.

questions.question: What metric is most commonly used to measure angular similarity between two normalized vectors?
questions.explanation: Cosine similarity calculates the cosine of the angle between two vectors, ranging from -1 to 1.

questions.question: What is 'overfitting' in machine learning?
options: When a model performs exceptionally on training data but poorly on unseen test data
When a dataset has too few rows to train an algorithm
When the model's loss function never decreases during training
When training completes faster than expected
questions.explanation: Overfitting happens when a model learns noise and specific training details rather than generalized patterns.

questions.question: In Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), what is the primary role of the vector database?
options: To train the foundational model from scratch
To retrieve the most relevant contextual documents based on user query similarity
To render HTML components in the frontend
To manage user passwords and JWT sessions
questions.explanation: The vector database performs fast similarity retrieval to pass relevant context chunks into the LLM prompt.

questions.question: Why is demographic data (such as gender, age, college tier) stripped in blind AI matching algorithms?
options: To prevent historical bias and ensure candidates are evaluated strictly on demonstrable skills
Because vector databases cannot store text
To make API calls run faster
questions.explanation: Stripping protected attributes prevents algorithmic bias and ensures evaluation is skills-first and fair.
